sections.title: A Principle I Want KoreVity to Follow

blocks.text: I want every business object to have the same "superpowers."
Every object—whether it's a Customer, Task, Invoice, or Document—should support:

items: Identity: A unique ID and its own profile.
Lifecycle: States such as Draft → Active → Completed → Archived.
History: A complete audit trail of changes.
Comments: Collaboration directly on the object.
Automation: The ability to trigger workflows.
Analytics: Metrics and KPIs related to that object.
Permissions: Control over who can view or edit it.
AI Assistance: Context-aware help, summaries, recommendations, or predictions where useful.

blocks.text: Because every object behaves consistently, users don't have to relearn the platform for each module. That consistency is one of the foundations of a great user experience.

blocks.text: Up until now, we've been thinking about objects.

blocks.text: This is one of the most strategically important layers.

sections.title: Next Phase: The Universal Object Page

blocks.text: Instead of designing a completely different interface for Customers, Orders, Inventory, Projects, Employees, Assets, and Suppliers...
We'll design one universal object layout that every business object inherits.
That means if a user learns how to navigate a Customer page once, they'll already know how to use an Order, Project, Product, Employee, or Shipment page.

This consistency will dramatically reduce the learning curve and make KoreVity feel like one cohesive platform rather than dozens of disconnected modules. From both a user experience and development perspective, it's one of the highest-leverage decisions we can make.
This chapter is probably one of the biggest architectural decisions we'll make.
If we get this right, KoreVity will feel like one unified platform forever.
It will eventually feel like Salesforce, SAP, or many ERPs—where every module feels like it was built by a different team.
We're going to avoid that completely.

sections.title: The KoreVity Design System

blocks.text: A complete design language that every screen, component, interaction, icon, spacing rule, animation, table, form, chart, AI panel, and future module follows.

This won't just make the software beautiful—it will make development dramatically faster because every future screen will be assembled from a library of reusable components instead of redesigned from scratch.

And there's another benefit: your public KoreVity website already establishes a premium, modern visual identity. By creating a formal design system next, we can ensure the software feels like a natural extension of the website rather than a separate product, while also applying what we've learned from the iPhone rendering issue to keep the application performant across all devices. That investment will pay off throughout the entire lifetime of the platform.
I genuinely think this will become one of the biggest assets KoreVity ever has.
Most startups treat design as something that happens in Figma.
Companies like Apple, Stripe, Linear, Notion, Shopify and GitHub don't.
After that, every screen becomes an assembly of proven building blocks.

blocks.text: While reviewing all of these objects, I noticed something that could become one of KoreVity's biggest strengths.
I think we should introduce a concept called Relationships as a first-class capability.
Today, many systems have relationships hidden in the database.
I think KoreVity should expose them.

sections.title: Phase 7.4 — Workflow Validation
sections.searchText: let's establish another permanent principle.

sections.title: Every workflow should move work forward with the least possible human effort while keeping humans in control of important decisions.

blocks.text: We're not trying to automate everything.
We're trying to automate everything that should be automated.
The important decisions still belong to people.

sections.searchText: notice the second part. we're not trying to automate everything. we're trying to automate everything that should be automated. the important decisions still belong to people.

sections.title: What is a Workflow?

blocks.text: A workflow is simply the journey from something happening to something being completed.
That order doesn't magically become a delivery.

sections.searchText: a workflow is simply the journey from something happening to something being completed. for example: a customer places an order. that order doesn't magically become a delivery. work happens. people become involved. approvals happen. inventory changes. invoices are generated. payments arrive. that's a workflow.

sections.title: Every Workflow Must Answer

blocks.text: Every workflow in KoreVity must answer these questions.
If we cannot answer all seven...

sections.searchText: every workflow in korevity must answer these questions. what starts it? what happens next? who is responsible? can anything happen automatically? what requires human approval? what completes it? what should be recorded? if we cannot answer all seven... the workflow isn't finished.

sections.title: Universal Workflow Pattern

blocks.text: After reviewing dozens of business systems, I think every workflow in KoreVity should follow one universal structure.

sections.searchText: after reviewing dozens of business systems, i think every workflow in korevity should follow one universal structure. trigger validation decision execution monitoring completion history every process. no exceptions.

sections.title: Stage 1 — Trigger
sections.searchText: something happens. examples: customer submits order. employee requests leave. inventory reaches minimum level. document uploaded. invoice overdue. task completed. machine reports failure. email received. everything starts with an event.

sections.title: Stage 2 — Validation

blocks.text: This prevents bad data from entering the system.

sections.searchText: before work begins. the system checks. examples. is the customer active? is stock available? does the employee have permission? is required information complete? should this be blocked? this prevents bad data from entering the system.

sections.title: Stage 3 — Decision

steps: Does a manager need to approve?

sections.searchText: this is important. not every workflow needs approval. some do. questions. can this happen automatically? should ai recommend something? does a manager need to approve? should finance review it? the workflow decides.

sections.title: Stage 4 — Execution
sections.searchText: now work actually happens. examples. reserve inventory. assign task. generate invoice. notify customer. update dashboard. schedule delivery. everything happens here.

sections.title: Stage 5 — Monitoring

blocks.text: This is where most software stops.

sections.searchText: this is where most software stops. korevity doesn't. questions. is the workflow progressing? is it delayed? is someone waiting? has sla expired? should reminders be sent? monitoring keeps workflows alive.

sections.title: Stage 6 — Completion

blocks.text: Because the business outcome has been achieved.
Order isn't complete because it was packed.
It's complete because it was delivered and confirmed.

sections.searchText: work finishes. not because someone clicked done. because the business outcome has been achieved. example. order isn't complete because it was packed. it's complete because it was delivered and confirmed. very different.

sections.title: Stage 7 — History
sections.searchText: nothing disappears. every workflow becomes organizational memory. later we can answer. who approved? when? how long? what changed? why was it delayed? history becomes intelligence.

sections.title: Human vs Automation

blocks.text: One of the biggest decisions we've made.

sections.searchText: one of the biggest decisions we've made. let's define the rule.

sections.title: Humans Decide
sections.searchText: humans should: approve budgets. approve discounts. approve hiring. approve contracts. resolve exceptions. handle relationships. exercise judgment.

sections.title: Automation Executes
sections.searchText: automation should: move data. create records. send notifications. generate reports. assign tasks. update statuses. schedule reminders. repeat boring work.

sections.title: AI Assists

blocks.text: Never secretly make important business decisions.

sections.searchText: ai should: summarize. recommend. predict. explain. prioritize. detect risks. suggest actions. never secretly make important business decisions.

sections.title: Exception Handling

blocks.text: Instead of pretending they won't, KoreVity should treat exceptions as first-class citizens.

blocks.text: Every workflow must pass these questions:

Can someone understand the workflow six months later?
